# Reference-event regression fixtures

These fixtures support Issue 12 regression tests without Earth Engine or network access.

## Cases

- `haiti-2021-ascending`: small ROI centred on the USGS 14 Aug 2021 M7.2 Nippes, Haiti event; exercises the ASCENDING model contract.
- `sumatra-2022-descending`: small ROI centred on the USGS 25 Feb 2022 M6.1 event near Bukittinggi, Indonesia; exercises the DESCENDING model contract.

The SAR-LRA study used Haiti (2021) and Sumatra (2022) as unseen-event evaluations. These fixtures use those public event locations only as stable geospatial anchors.

## Important data provenance

The GeoTIFF pixel values are **synthetic, project-authored Sentinel-1-like dB values** generated by `generate_fixtures.py`. They are not copied from Copernicus/Sentinel-1 products and must not be interpreted as observations of either earthquake.

The synthetic fixture data are distributed under the repository MIT licence. The public earthquake metadata are factual references from USGS event pages.

The files intentionally include:

- four bands in the production order `postVV, postVH, diffVV, diffVH`;
- 10 m projected pixels;
- orbit metadata;
- a small NoData corner;
- enough spatial variation to produce both below- and above-threshold regression windows with the deterministic test model.

`*.expected.json` is the committed regression baseline. Update it only when a reviewed preprocessing/inference change intentionally changes results.
